result.rationale: The diff shows in GoogleCalendarService deleteEvent: `const calendarId = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;` — in the fallback branch externalCalendarId is falsy, so find compares each cal.externalId to a falsy value and can never match, yielding undefined. Pre-refactor code used `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. The same self-comparison defect exists in updateEvent. This is a real regression verifiable directly from the diff.

judged_text: deleteEvent has the same self-comparison fallback (`find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` evaluated only when externalCalendarId is falsy), so `calendarId` resolves to undefined and the delete call fails. Cancellations of Google Calendar events without an externalCalendarId on the booking reference no longer delete the event — orphaned events remain on hosts' calendars and Google returns an error for the undefined calendar id, where the pre-refactor code used `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`.
